Hi Elena / Tom,

Appreciate the RFP and the clarity on your patterns. Quick framing below — I'll pull Ben (solutions) and Marissa (commercial) into the thread for numbers and a MAP.

Three pragmatic packaging options we typically propose for VPC/on-prem customers:

1) Pilot (90 days) — Starter Platform: 
   - Small platform fee (one-time onboarding + monthly platform fee)
   - Metered consumption for GPUs/serving (per-token and per-embedding)
   - Standard support (business hours, next-business-day response)
   - Purpose: de-risk and validate perf/cost.

2) Commit + Amortized Platform Fee — Production:
   - 12–36 month reserved capacity commit (GPU node-months)
   - Platform fee can be amortized / reduced against commit (we've done up to 40% offset for large, multi-year commits)
   - Tiered support (Priority with 2-hour incident response, or Dedicated SRE add-on)
   - Automatic fallback routing & regional failover included.

3) Hybrid (Anchor + Burst) — Large deployments:
   - Anchor commit for baseline capacity + metered burst for peaks
   - Negotiated platform fee cap and true-up cadence
   - Implementation credits available in exchange for longer commits or faster PO timelines.

Support mapping (summary):
- Standard: business hours, 8x5, 24h for Sev1 triage.
- Priority: 24x7, 2h initial response for Sev1, 4h for Sev2, monthly ops review.
- Dedicated SRE: SLA-backed runbooks, dedicated escalation channel, quarterly runbooks and 40 SRE hours/month (negotiable).

Next steps I propose:
- Ben, can you put together a short pricing worksheet and two example scenarios (12m commit, 36m commit) and show platform fee offsets and implementation credit tradeoffs?
- Marissa, please confirm typical amortization windows we can propose and any standard contract caveats.
- I'll draft a simple MAP (milestones: pilot -> pilot success -> PO -> deployment -> cutover) and share a DocuSign draft addendum for the offset credit.

I've attached a one-page pricing checklist that procurement typically finds useful.

Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Camila — high level numbers below to get the conversation moving. I'll put a proper worksheet into Drive and flag assumptions.

Assumptions (to validate): 18M tokens/mo baseline, 2 regions, 1:4 ratio live:batch. Pilot = 3 node-months reserved equivalent. Production scenarios modeled:

A) 12-month commit (baseline 24 node-months / month)
   - Platform fee: $45k/month baseline (standard)
   - Offset: up to 30% platform fee reduction if customer prepays 9 months of commit within 30 days of signature.
   - Implementation credits: 240 hours (applied over first 6 months) in exchange for 15% additional offset.

B) 36-month commit (baseline 24 node-months/month)
   - Platform fee: $40k/month baseline
   - Offset: up to 40% (amortized across 36 months) for multi-year anchor commit + on-prem licensing guarantee
   - Implementation credits: 480 hours in exchange for 25% extra offset + extended support retainer at reduced monthly rate.

SLA credit / rollback protection: we can include a 3-tier SLA credit schedule (service availability thresholds) and a one-time migration credit if customer elects to move off Redwood within first 12 months (pro-rated).

Trade idea to give procurement: Exchange implementation credits (professional services) for platform-fee offset. Implementation credits are easier to book and are frequently acceptable to procurement as they appear as services.

I'll upload a spreadsheet (with line-item math) and a suggested draft addendum for the DocuSign link Camila mentioned.

Ben
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Elena / Tom — thanks, and great questions. TL;DR below plus attachments and links.

1) Migration credit formula (pro-rated):
   - If Stellarsys elects to fully migrate off Redwood within 12 months of production cutover, Redwood will provide a one-time migration credit equal to 20% of remaining committed platform fee value at time of termination (cap $150k). Credit applied as a refund or to final invoice per the ordered payment method.

2) SLA credit table (proposal):
   - Availability >= 99.95%: no credit
   - 99.5% <= Availability < 99.95%: 5% monthly platform fee credit
   - 99.0% <= Availability < 99.5%: 10% monthly platform fee credit
   - Availability < 99.0%: 25% monthly platform fee credit + 1:1 engineering uplift credit for documented incident root cause (up to 2 weeks SRE support).

3) DocuSign addendum & MAP:
   - I've drafted a short addendum that documents the offset window, amortization approach, and the migration credit formula — link to DocuSign: https://docusign.com/Envelope/ABC-123-stellarsys
